extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies preparing CAA section 111(d) state plans, EPA staff, regulated power plant owners/operators, environmental lawyers and consultants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for states to develop and submit state plans under CAA section 111(d) implementing emission guidelines for existing electric generating units (EGUs), including use of RULOF, unit of standards, compliance flexibilities, reporting, and enforceable commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RULOF to apply less stringent standard
rubrics_metrics.description: States may invoke RULOF to apply a less stringent standard of performance to a particular affected EGU when the state demonstrates that the EGU cannot reasonably achieve the degree of emission limitation determined by the EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that case, the state plan may not necessarily achieve the same stringency as each source achieving the EPA's presumptive standards of performance because affected EGUs for which RULOF has been invoked would have standards of performance less stringent than the EPA's presumptive standards. See section X.C.2 of the preamble and 40 CFR 60.24a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence demonstration for alternative methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Should a state decide to establish a standard of performance for an affected EGU using a methodology other than that provided by the EPA in these emission guidelines, the state would have to demonstrate that the resulting standard of performance achieves equivalent emission reductions as application of the EPA's presumptive standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States proposing a different methodology must provide demonstration/documentation showing equivalent emissions reductions compared to EPA's presumptive approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units for standards of performance by subcategory
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumptive standards of performance for coal-fired steam-generating affected EGUs and base load and intermediate load natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating affected EGUs are in units of lb CO2/MWh; the presumptive standard of performance for low-load natural gas-fired and oil-fired affected EGUs are in units of lb CO2/MMBtu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any standards of performance pursuant to consideration of RULOF must be determined in these same units as appropriate to the subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF stringency floor (40 CFR 60.24a(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: 40 CFR 60.24a(f) requires that a standard of performance pursuant to consideration of RULOF be no less stringent than necessary to address the fundamental difference identified under 40 CFR 60.24a(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: If an affected EGU can install and operate CCS but only at such a low CO2 capture rate that it could reasonably achieve greater stringency based on natural gas co-firing, the state would apply a standard of performance based on natural gas co-firing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of operating conditions relied on for RULOF as enforceable requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating conditions within the control of a designated facility that are relied on for purposes of RULOF must be included as enforceable requirements in state plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reliance on facility operating conditions is the predicate for receiving a particular standard of performance, adherence to those commitments is necessary to maintain the level of emission reduction required. See 40 CFR 60.24a(g) and related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: State commitment to cease operation when predicate for standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with CAA section 111(d)(1), state plans must include commitments to cease operation as necessary for the implementation and enforcement of standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such commitments are the predicate for receiving a particular standard of performance, the commitments must be enforceable (e.g., retirement dates included in state plans become federally enforceable upon EPA approval). See examples in prior EPA actions (Affordable Clean Energy Rule; best available retrofit technology examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone reporting requirements for certain EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: The milestone reporting requirements for affected coal-fired steam generating EGUs in the medium-term subcategory and those relying on a shorter remaining useful life for a less-stringent standard of performance pursuant to RULOF are authorized under both CAA sections 114(a) and 111(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting requirements are necessary to ensure that the predicate conditions for the sources' standards of performance are satisfied; states should include appropriate milestone reporting in plans where relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance flexibilities must have consistent compliance demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the state plan incorporates compliance flexibilities like emission averaging and trading, an affected EGU must demonstrate compliance consistent with the expression of the respective flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section X.D of the preamble for more information; states that adopt averaging/trading must specify how compliance is demonstrated in the aggregate or for individual sources as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and historical precedent for trading/averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has authorized trading or averaging as compliance methods in several emission guidelines and implementing regulations, and in recent final emission guidelines for other industries the Agency allowed states to demonstrate compliance in the aggregate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may rely on this precedent when designing trading/averaging programs, but must ensure the compliance demonstration aligns with the approved expression of the flexibility (and with any statutory or administrative constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted consideration of 'other factors' beyond costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA reiterates that states are not precluded from considering information and factors other than costs under 40 CFR 60.24a(e)(ii) and (iii). 'Other factors' may include facility-specific circumstances and factors that the EPA did not anticipate and consider in the applicable emission guideline that make achieving the EPA's degree of emission limitation unreasonable for that facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States seeking less-stringent standards under RULOF can present facility-specific evidence or other unanticipated factors to justify adjustments, consistent with the regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability mechanisms and limited extensions for retirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanism described in the preamble (section X.C.1.d) is not restricted to circumstances in which a state needs to provide an affected EGU additional time to comply specifically for reliability, but it can be used for this purpose. The reliability mechanism described in section XII.F.3.b is specific to reliability and can be used to extend the date by which a source plans to cease operating by up to 1 year. States may also elect to include the short-term reliability mechanism described in section XII.F.3.a in their plans to address grid emergency situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that include these mechanisms must specify the conditions under which extensions apply and ensure consistency with plan enforceability and the emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline emission rate definition for existing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline emission rate for existing sources is the CO2 mass emissions and corresponding electricity generation data for a given affected EGU from any continuous 8-quarter period from 40 CFR part 75 reporting within the 5-year period immediately prior to the date the final rule is published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and sources should use this definition when calculating baseline emission rates for determining standards and compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, mass-balance, and leakage assessment for CO2 storage (subpart RR and VV / ISO 27916:2019)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both subpart RR and subpart VV (CSA/ANSI ISO 27916:2019) require an assessment and monitoring of potential leakage pathways; quantification of inputs, losses, and storage through a mass balance approach; and documentation of steps and approaches used to establish these quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary differences relate to the terms in their respective mass balance equations, how each defines leakage, and when facilities may discontinue reporting. States/facilities implementing CO2 storage via EOR or other approaches should follow the applicable standard's monitoring, quantification, and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of enforceable retirement dates and reliance on commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Retirement dates or enforceable shutdown commitments that are relied on to support a less-stringent standard must be included in state plans and become federally enforceable upon EPA approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past EPA actions required retirement dates to be federally enforceable in SIPs or state plans; states should ensure that any reliance on retirements or shutdown commitments is documented and enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to express standards/limits in statutory/regulatory units
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the presumptive standards are expressed in specific units (lb CO2/MWh or lb CO2/MMBtu), any state-determined standard (including under RULOF) must be expressed in the applicable units so comparisons and compliance demonstrations are consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves comparability between EPA presumptive standards and state-adopted standards; conversion approaches should be documented where necessary.
